note: A lightweight decision log. Mutating JSON loses history; this keeps it, so the model can answer 'why do we believe this?' rather than only 'what do we believe?'.

decisions.subject: vehicle.tundra.disposition
decisions.reason: The Tundra will transport Lane, Klein and Tilly. Vehicle ownership will be reassessed after California daily-life evidence exists.

decisions.subject: career.cherie_role.title
decisions.previous_value: Senior Product Manager II (treated as settled)
decisions.reason: The interview itinerary and the recruiting context disagree on level. Guessing a title would set compensation expectations on an unverified premise.

decisions.subject: launch_fund.floor
decisions.new_value: $10,000 as an activation floor, with a computed ladder above it
decisions.reason: The common physical move alone models to about $14,019, and the base transition to about $19,154. Treating the floor as the budget would have made the move look funded when it was not.

decisions.subject: scenario.dimensions
decisions.previous_value: House branch shown inside the Path A/B/C columns
decisions.new_value: Career path, house branch and employer support modeled as independent dimensions
decisions.reason: A career path never selects a house branch. Embedding one in the other hides nine real combinations behind three.

decisions.subject: career.opportunities
decisions.previous_value: Two Cherie-related records that looked like duplicates
decisions.new_value: Two separate threads, one on hold pending its requisition ID
decisions.reason: Merging recruiting threads on a guess destroys the ability to tell which process actually advanced.

decisions.subject: house.orlando.disposition
decisions.reason: Lane leans toward selling, but PM quotes, the CMA and the replacement inspection are all outstanding. A lean is not evidence, so the branch stays unresolved and the model keeps pricing all three.
decisions.review_after: After PM quotes, CMA and inspection land
